knowledge: Users are named in questions by their display name (or by id: "user no. 3025" is the UserId). A post/comment belongs to its owner (OwnerUserId); "the user who last edited" is the last-editor id.

CreationDate / LastAccessDate are datetimes; a question's date such as 2014/9/1 or 2014/4/23 is a calendar date (the year part alone scopes a year). "The latest" event / "acquired the first" badge are MAX / MIN over the corresponding date, and "during 2010" means the year of the date is 2010.

A post's Title is its title and its body is the post text; a comment's content is the comment text. A question quoting a phrase (a post title or a comment) refers to the record whose text equals that phrase.

Metric semantics (dataset commonsense evidence): comment score is 0-100 and above 60 means a positive comment; higher view count means higher popularity; more favorites means a more valuable post; a tag with more counts is more popular. Reputation: the user with higher reputation has more influence. Age bands: teenager 13-18, adult 19-65, elder over 65. A user's badges are the badge records obtained (e.g. Autobiographer, Student).
A tag is named by its tag name, and posts carry tags; a tag points to its excerpt post and wiki post.
"The most valuable post" is the one with the highest favorite count; "the most viewed" the highest view count; "the highest score" the highest score.

Percentages put one set of the same entities on both sides of the fraction (count of the entities satisfying the condition / count of the entities in scope, times 100); the count is taken at the entity's own granularity (a user or a post counted once).
